checks: Matched raw source 185fb6155f830e0e at its declared digest. Its §§1–2, (1)–(4), contain the common affine level, base-independent normalization, simultaneous finite weak convergence, and joint inequality with its census. The specific coarea formula in (2) is an example of the common multiplier; the rank-drop assumption in (3) is stated for the subsequent lift and is unused here.

For fixed j the positive-mass compact portions lie in parallel N-planes. Translating them to their common direction space and translating the output by the corresponding weighted origin preserves all N-volumes. Convexity of D_j and affinity of the single cut put the Minkowski sum in the integer output slice. Multiplication by alpha_j^(1/N) works on both sides because alpha_j is independent of the base.

An open epsilon-neighborhood of each compact input has eventual positive prelimit mass by lower Portmanteau. Compact inner approximation within each input slice is valid for finite Euclidean Borel measures. The weighted sum lies in the closed epsilon-neighborhood of the output compact because the positive weights sum to one.

Upper Portmanteau gives limit output mass at least the limsup of prelimit output masses for that fixed closed neighborhood. Each prelimit lower bound has liminf at least the sum of the powered positive limit input masses, by lower Portmanteau and finiteness of the number of inputs. Letting epsilon decrease to zero uses continuity from above of the finite output measure, without a boundary-null assumption or convergence of the plane directions.

The zero extensions are legitimate: an integer output outside P has every prelimit fiber empty and hence the identically zero limit. It cannot satisfy the derived strictly positive lower bound. Any integer point of conv(P_+) has a finite convex representation with its zero coefficients removed. The cases of one input, repeated bases, n=0, and N=1 need no exceptions.

overlap.comparison: Its proof (32)–(35) passes a multiplicative log-concavity inequality for one sequence of densities to one weak limit. It does not give the additive 1/N-power inequality between distinct lattice-base limits, the common slice scaling, or the positive base census.

Its proof (20)–(23) also uses Portmanteau through possible affine dimension loss, for the multiplicative log-concavity of a single weak limit. The distinct-base output and lattice census here do not follow from that closure result.
Its compatible-fiber equivalence works at the level of compact sets and does not imply the cross-fiber measure inequality under weak convergence.

readability: The common multiplier may vary arbitrarily with j; only its independence from the base is used. The weak limits are assumed to exist, and no statement identifies them with a particular rate law.

summary: One common normalization and one affine cut at each step yield the joint N-dimensional inequality, which passes to the simultaneous weak limits. Positivity at every integer output proves the exact lattice census.
